items.title: Gaurav Bhatia files ₹2 crore defamation case in Delhi HC against CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka
items.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and Senior Advocate Gaurav Bhatia has filed a defamation case before the Delhi High Court against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and its leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Bhatia has sought ₹2 crore in damages and an injunction against the CJP leaders. He sued the CJP and its leaders after an AI-generated graphic falsely attributed remarks about Swatantra Bhardwaj to Bhatia. Bhardwaj is accused of assault on the father of CJP activist Nishu Azad. The post stated that Bhatia called Bhardwaj a "dimagi naxal". Das shared the graphic on X, prompting Bhatia to deny making the remarks and give him 24 hours to delete the post and issue an unconditional apology. Das, who later deleted the post, clarified on his X account that it was AI-generated, but asked Bhatia whether he “disagreed” with the AI-generated statement. CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka allegedly amplified the disputed post by reposting the graphic from Das's account, adding a caption mocking BJP leaders. Ranka had earlier joined Das and other CJP members in demanding action against Bharadwaj over an alleged assault on the father of CJP activist Nishu Azad.

items.title: Supreme Court directs Centre, States to set up 449 exclusive NDPS courts within 6 months
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Central government, States, and Union Territories to take immediate steps to establish 449 exclusive courts for trial of cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (NDPS Act). A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana issued the directive after taking on record a status report filed by the Union of India, which revealed that only 176 of the required 449 exclusive NDPS courts are presently operational across the country. The Court expressed concern over the alarming surge in narcotics cases nationwide and directed setting up 449 courts, preferably within six months. “Having regard to the current pendency of cases under the NDPS Act and the alarming increase in offences under the Act across the country, it is expedient and in the interest of justice that the requisite 449 exclusive NDPS courts be established at the earliest,” the Court recorded. The bench directed all States and Union Territories to urgently arrange the necessary court infrastructure and appoint judicial and administrative staff to bridge the deficit. items.title: Marital Rape case: Supreme Court to decide hearing date on September 9
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to immediately defer the hearing in the batch of petitions challenging the marital rape exception. The Court rejected the request to postpone the hearing till November. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana stated that it will hear the Union government on Wednesday, September 9, before fixing a date for final arguments. Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler passed the order. Delhi Police told the Court that the anticipatory bail plea was not maintainable and that there should not be any apprehension that just because a case has been registered, Bharti would be arrested. items.title: Senior Advocate DLN Rao passes away
items.summary: Senior Advocate DLN Rao , a veteran member of the Karnataka Bar and one of the country’s leading lawyers in mining law, passed away on Monday. Rao was a designated Senior Advocate of the Karnataka High Court and with more that five decades of experience at the bar. He had an extensive practice before the Karnataka High Court as well as the Supreme Court, particularly in matters concerning mining, land acquisition, infrastructure and public law. Rao is one of the foremost authorities in mining law. Rao also played a notable role in litigation surrounding Bengaluru's Namma Metro project. In 2010, the Karnataka High Court appointed him as amicus curiae in proceedings concerning the proposed underground Metro stretch between the Vidhana Soudha and the High Court through the Cubbon Park area. The Bench had sought his assistance considering the wider implications of the project. The High Court subsequently permitted the underground Metro project while imposing safeguards concerning restoration of land and protection of the green cover. items.title: Unemployed woman's land cannot be assumed to be joint family asset: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently observed that the mere fact that a woman was unemployed and had no independent source of income is not sufficient to hold that property purchased in her name was acquired from joint-family funds [ Rajesh Exports v B Devaraj ]. The Bench of Justices Jayant Banerji and Tara Vitasta Ganju made the observation while setting aside a 2009 trial court decree passed in favour of two sons and the wife of one S Balasubramanya over certain property in Bengaluru. Balasubramanya had inherited the said property from his mother, Lalithamma. In 2004, he sold the property to a company, Rajesh Exports. Balasubramanya went missing shortly thereafter. His two sons and wife (plaintiffs), however, challenged the sale of the property to Rajesh Exports. They argued that the land was a joint family asset in which they held rights, and which could not have been unilaterally sold by Balasubramanya. They filed a suit before a civil court asserting a share in the said property. Advocate Siddharth Sharma appeared for the NGO before Justice Tushar Rao Gedela on September 3 and said he had instructions to withdraw the case.
